title: The HD 93683 drift gives an outer-period limit of 4.3 years at quadrupole order for M12 = 33, m3 = 8-25 solar masses and e2 <= 0.5
abstract: We use published inclination drifts of HD 93683 and HD 303514 to test their third-body models. We derive the largest possible sky-inclination rate from the standard double-averaged quadrupole torque. The bound includes inner eccentricity and does not require a known outer orientation. For HD 93683, the reported rate of 0.325 degrees per year, inner period of 17.8 days, eccentricity of 0.27, inner mass of 33 solar masses, third-star mass of 8-25 solar masses and outer eccentricity at most 0.5 give an outer-period ceiling of 4.25 years. The ceiling is 3.42 years for a circular outer orbit and 6.47 years if the third-star mass is unrestricted. Exact Newtonian averages over fixed orbits differ from the quadrupole rate by at most 0.69 percent in 36 tested cases with outer periods of 4-12 years. In 48 three-body integrations, a 12-year outer orbit can have short normal-speed peaks above the reported drift, but the largest 36-year inclination slope is only 0.043 degrees per year. Short peaks therefore give a weak test of a steady drift. We also derive a joint torque and radial-velocity test. In the circular-inner model for HD 303514 with inner mass of 5 solar masses, any 4-year companion orbit needs a binary-centre velocity amplitude of at least 7.72 km/s for outer eccentricity zero, or 5.61 km/s for outer eccentricity 0.5, after minimization over third-star mass and orientation. These are conditional bounds, not companion detections. We use prior aggregate measurements and do not refit photometry. Larger outer eccentricity, a different inner model, other torques, and the real time sampling require further tests. Code, synthetic trajectories, source hashes and reproduction instructions are included.

display.caption: Conditional companion constraints. Left: the largest secular outer period for HD 93683, for inner mass 33 solar masses, inner eccentricity 0.27 and drift 0.325 degrees per year. The shaded mass range is 8-25 solar masses. Right: the smallest binary-centre radial-velocity amplitude for HD 303514 in the circular-inner model with inner mass 5 solar masses and drift 0.102 degrees per year. Each curve minimizes over all third-star masses and outer orientations. These curves use double-averaged Newtonian quadrupole dynamics.

Three-body examples with third-star mass 25 solar masses, initial mutual angle 45 degrees, inner eccentricity 0.27 and outer eccentricity 0.5. The outer periods are 4, 8 and 12 years. Left: inclination change for one fixed observer, initially at 85 degrees. The dashed line is the published drift, shown as a reference. Right: the sampled instantaneous speed of the inner orbit normal. Short peaks above the reference rate can occur even when the long-term inclination slope is small. Initial outer mean anomaly and argument of pericentre are zero. These examples are diagnostic; they are not fits to the observed light curves.
